body:
Leaving or reopening the log viewer can leave a blocked reader or stale stream ownership behind. Own Logcat children through cancellation and stream cleanup, subscribe before reading, and prevent an old completion from clearing a newer stream. Keep the supported API21 commands/PID filter, portable export filename, and bounded log windows with explicit omission notices.

Following the review feedback, `9f95cb57` inlines viewer startup with the normal lifecycle launch default and restores unused general Process extensions to their upstream behavior. The existing inner subscription is installed before the reader starts; a cancelled lifecycle does not enter the outer task. Cancellation and finalization share one release operation, so process destruction is not repeated. The reader keeps standard `use` exception handling; fallback stream closing remains necessary to unblock cancellation. Cleanup retains the primary failure and a small cancellation-cause handling step required by an assertions-enabled cancellation regression test; the generic exception-graph machinery is removed. The extra fixed deployment-log timeouts are also removed.

Validation for this revision:

- 46 Process/Logcat/LogBuffer cases pass with JVM assertions enabled. Their tested inputs are unchanged at this head; the LogView follow-up is checked separately by source review, style and CI. These cases cover real child cancellation, IO parallelism one, cancellation before reader entry, single release and primary-error propagation.
- Style and patch checks pass.
- [Current upstream PR CI](https://github.com/osfans/trime/actions/runs/39900491225): 5/5 jobs passed; application unit-test and Lint tasks executed. The CI merge and targeted host tests are separate scopes; no exported full-application testcase count is inferred.

[Current source, original results and limits](https://github.com/X2M7/trime/blob/599b26cfbbec22f753ce421fe1d7abf895cf7d00/doc/contribution-split/checks/review-slim-20261023/README.md) are outside this application patch. Ownership guarantees apply to the Logcat path, not the restored general extensions. No 2/5-second deployment limit, new Android runtime, performance, Release or zero-warning acceptance is claimed; earlier device results remain historical.
